LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope contains only standard variable definitions and a source array. The `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `_filename`, `epoch`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, and all other variables are plain assignments with no command execution. The `source` array references the project's own GitHub release (`https://github.com/dee-dee-catorce/desksaw/releases/download/v$pkgver/deskSaw030LINUX.zip`) plus two local data files (`$pkgname.desktop` and `newlogo.png`) — this is normal AUR packaging. The `sha256sums` array includes two `SKIP` entries, which per the instructions is never grounds to fail this gate since no sources are downloaded or verified during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. There are no `eval`, `curl|bash`, `wget|bash`, base64-encoded blobs, or other suspicious command executions at the top level. The `package()` function is defined but never executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` (per the gate's narrow scope). No code in the top-level scope downloads and runs an untrusted payload or exfiltrates data.

The package's build logic (cp, chmod, ln, install) resides inside the `package()` function and is standard Arch packaging practice. Nothing in the sourcing phase deviates from benign variable assignments and array definitions.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard PKGBUILD — no top-level code execution risk
</summary>
</security_assessment>
